optimize_reason: Champion (CFO-margin annual change, Sharpe 1.38) retested under industry neutralization instead of subindustry: isolates whether the cash-generation improvement effect is peer-group-specific or a broad sector-level repricing.

Return-on-assets trend (net income / total assets annual change) at market-level grouping; the subindustry and industry variants of this ratio are already exhausted in the ledger, so market is the only untested cross-section.

Cash return on assets (CFO / total assets) annual change at industry level: the strongest cash-flow numerator moved onto the balance-sheet denominator, testing whether asset-scaled cash generation beats revenue-scaled.

EBIT margin annual change without the winsorize wrapper (the winsorized variant is already in the ledger): operating profitability trend before financing and tax effects, the cleanest read on core margin expansion.
EBIT on assets annual change: combines operating profitability with asset base, separating margin expansion from asset-heavy growth.
Operating-income margin annual change: narrower than EBIT (excludes non-operating items), a purer test of whether the market prices core operating leverage improvement.
Return on equity trend (net income / book equity annual change): tests whether shareholders' capital productivity improvement is priced differently from asset- or revenue-scaled profitability.
Cash flow on book equity annual change: pairs the winning cash-flow numerator with the equity denominator, isolating cash generation per unit of shareholder capital.

Gross margin annual change (revenue minus COGS over revenue): the most upstream profitability ratio, testing whether the effect starts at the cost-of-goods level rather than at the operating or bottom line.
Memory-axis probe on the champion: shorten the annual-change window from 252 to 200 trading days to test whether a slightly faster comparison baseline sharpens the cash-margin surprise.
Memory-axis probe in the other direction: lengthen to 300 days, testing whether a slower baseline filters out single-quarter cash-flow noise and raises Sharpe.

Benchmark structure (net margin annual change, Sharpe 1.44 at subindustry) retested at market-level grouping: the last untested cross-section for the single strongest known expression in this campaign.
Replace the champion's outer peer-ranking with demeaning neutralization: tests whether the effect survives as a continuous residual rather than a within-peer ordinal rank.

Swap the point-to-point annual difference for a rank transform over the same window: measures where current cash margin sits inside its own one-year distribution, immune to the scale of one-off cash swings.

Execution-order probe: smooth the cash leg and the earnings leg separately before subtracting, instead of differencing the composite gap. Prior campaigns showed this ordering can flip the signal sign, so the mirror ordering of the accrual-gap structure must be tested explicitly.
Exponential-decay smoothing applied after the annual cash-margin change: a turnover-reduction wrapper intended to lift Fitness without consuming a new fingerprint axis.
Gross-profit accrual leg (intfvm_prgs) on revenue at industry level; the subindustry variant is already in the ledger, so this completes the cross-section axis for that numerator.
Operating-profit accrual leg (intfvm_ipos) on revenue with peer ranking; only the neutralized variant is in the ledger, so the ranked form is still untested.
Free cash flow (CFO minus capex) scaled by assets instead of revenue: tests the Titman over-investment channel on the balance-sheet denominator, where the revenue-scaled form is already recorded.

Capital-expenditure intensity trend (capex / revenue annual change): the investment-discipline mirror of the profitability family, testing whether shrinking or expanding capex intensity is what the market rewards.
